page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It includes no local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions, and AVX-512 Bfloat16, though it lacks Advanced Matrix Extensions.

Benchmark results place the ecs.c4.2xlarge in the average tier for most CPU-bound tasks. The single-core stress-ng score is 1575.79, and the multi-core score is 8310.78. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1259.0 and a multi-core score of 4720.0. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is average at 464.83 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to a weak 37.74 GB/sec. Similarly, the Passmark memory score of 1525.1 and database operations score of 2280.27 are categorized as weak, indicating potential bottlenecks in memory-intensive operations.

The instance exhibits performance limitations under memory-bound and complex simulation workloads. Passmark CPU physics testing is weak at 736.01, and LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model are poor, delivering 11.72 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 5.16 tokens/sec for text generation. However, it maintains average performance for static web serving at 7.7 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 8.09 million operations per second. This profile makes the instance suitable for compute-heavy workloads with low memory footprints, such as software compilation, text processing, and basic web serving.

The CPU supports AVX-512 extensions but lacks AMX.
